title: Sparse per-task probes and optional Parallel Emission
body:
# Sparse per-task probes and optional Parallel Emission

Vocabulary follows [CONTEXT.md](../../CONTEXT.md). Do not merge [PR #48](https://github.com/NanmiCoder/dsh-agent-teams/pull/48) as-is.

## Test seams

Prefer two existing seams. Do not add a new polling service or a per-task `status` tool.

1. **Team scheduler** — `kickTeam` / `kickMember`, Attempt Start (`beginTaskAttempt`), and the existing `agent/status` idle edge. Next Probe At, Silent Kick, Captain Wake, and Mailbox Wake all hang off this seam. Inject a clock in tests.
2. **Protocol policy** — captain usage section (assembled live), member persona (spawn snapshot), assignment prompt, Status Probe / create-task tool copy, and the AgentTeams settings section that only flips Parallel Emission.

If these seams are wrong, say so before implementation. The Activity View stays a consumer of snapshots; it is not a probe clock.

## Problem Statement

Running a team burns a large share of tokens on repeated Status Probes. The captain protocol currently tells the model to poll until every task is terminal. Members often split claim, in_progress, completed, and the captain report across extra ReAct steps. After work is done, models still emit recap turns.

Users watching the Activity View already see Task Records and Member Liveness. Ending a Captain Turn does not stop the team or freeze the panel, but the protocol does not say that, so captains keep polling. If the captain instead goes idle and never Probes, a member that stays running on an open task, or a completion report that only reached the mailbox, can sit unnoticed by the captain model even though the human can see it.

A related GitHub change tried to fix the waste with prompt bans, sleep, and relaxed dependency checks. Those bans did not hold, and they removed the Status Probe recovery kick that idle members still need.

Separately, some models can put several AgentTeams tool calls in one assistant message (Parallel Emission). That saves steps even when exclusive tools still run in order. The agent-loop execution pool is a different knob and must not be overloaded. Parallel Emission should be opt-in, default off, and visible in plugin configuration.

## Solution

Keep three pictures of progress: Task Record and Member Liveness are real; the Activity View is the human projection and may lag. Captains may end a Captain Turn after dispatch and wait for Wake. They must not poll Status Probe in a loop or sleep-wait.

Each open attempt carries Next Probe At on the Task Record. Attempt Start arms it (ten minutes, not a user setting). A successful task update or a completion report for that task clears it. When due, runtime performs Silent Kick first. Captain Wake happens only if the task is still non-terminal and the assignee is still running or gone. Idle members that still own open work stay on the existing scheduler retry. After a Wake, re-arm; do not Wake in a tight loop.

Mailbox Wake is independent: if the captain is idle and the captain mailbox has unread reports, Wake soon. Do not wait for Next Probe At.

Parallel Emission is a boolean in the AgentTeams settings namespace, default false, shown as a checkbox on the Plugins configuration card for this plugin. When on, captain usage, new member personas, and assignment prompts may allow several AgentTeams tool calls in one response. Existing member personas stay as spawned. Dependency ids must still exist; same-response creates rely on exclusive in-order execution.

## User Stories

1. As a user, I want the Activity View to keep showing live members after the captain stops calling tools, so that ending a Captain Turn does not look like the team died.
2. As a user, I want the Activity View to stay independent of whether the create card is on screen, so that I can watch work in a long transcript.
3. As a user, I want Task Record progress and Member Liveness composed into the Activity View, so that I can tell “queued” from “actually running”.
4. As a user, I want to leave the captain idle without the panel freezing, so that I can read the DAG while members work.
5. As a captain, I want to end a Captain Turn after tasks exist, so that I do not burn cache_read waiting.
6. As a captain, I want member completion messages to Wake me, so that I can present results without polling.
7. As a captain, I want to stay in the turn and send guidance when I choose, so that ending the turn is allowed rather than required.
8. As a captain, I want protocol text that does not tell me to poll Status Probe until every task is terminal, so that I stop empty status loops.
9. As a captain, I want protocol text that forbids bash sleep as a wait, so that I do not add sleep+status cycles.
10. As a captain, I want to call Status Probe at most as a diagnostic, so that one snapshot can still kick recovery.
11. As a captain, I want create-task results to say the assignee was notified, so that I do not send_message only to dispatch.
12. As a captain, I want to omit a recap after delete, so that the last turn is not a polite summary.
13. As a member, I want assignment messages to include the attempt id, so that I can update the current generation.
14. As a member, I want not to poll Status Probe for new work, so that I wait for assignment Wakes instead.
15. As a member, I want a one-shot Status Probe only if I am blocked, so that I still have a diagnostic.
16. As a member, I want prerequisite outputs inline on assignment when dependencies completed, so that I do not read team.json to start a review.
17. As a user, I want idle members who still own open work to be retried without a Captain Turn, so that Silent Kick covers the common stall.
18. As a user, I want a member that stays running on a non-terminal task to eventually produce a Captain Wake, so that the captain can reassign or interrupt.
19. As a user, I want that Wake to happen only after Silent Kick, so that the scheduler gets the first chance.
20. As a user, I want a missing or unknown assignee treated like a running hang after Silent Kick, so that a vanished member is not ignored.
21. As a user, I want Next Probe At stored on each Task Record, so that two tasks do not share one countdown.
22. As a captain, I do not want to keep Next Probe At in the prompt, so that the clock survives model non-compliance.
23. As a user, I want Attempt Start to arm Next Probe At, so that claimed work gets a due time.
24. As a user, I want a successful update_task on that attempt to clear Next Probe At, so that healthy progress does not Wake the captain.
25. As a user, I want a completion report for that task to clear Next Probe At, so that finished work is not probed.
26. As a user, I want the default arm interval to be ten minutes and not a settings field, so that plugin configuration stays one Parallel Emission checkbox.
27. As a user, I want a Captain Wake to re-arm Next Probe At, so that a still-stuck task is not woken every scheduler tick.
28. As a user, I want no Captain Wake loop, so that a hanging member cannot burn cache_read every few seconds.
29. As a captain, I want Mailbox Wake when I am idle and have unread captain mail, so that a failed live steer still delivers the report.
30. As a captain, I want Mailbox Wake without waiting for Next Probe At, so that a finished report is not hidden for ten minutes.
31. As a user, I want Status Probe to remain a whole-team snapshot plus kick, so that we do not invent a per-task status tool.
32. As a user, I want the Activity View poll unchanged, so that human display is not the probe clock.
33. As a user, I want Parallel Emission off by default, so that models that only emit one tool call keep the serial protocol.
34. As a user, I want a Plugins configuration checkbox labelled for Parallel Emission on the AgentTeams card, so that I can opt in without opening Agent Loop settings.
35. As a user, I want that checkbox not to write maxParallelToolCalls, so that the execution pool stays on the Agent Loop card.
36. As a captain, I want usage text to allow several create_task calls in one response when Parallel Emission is on, so that one step can build the graph.
37. As a captain, I want later create_task calls in that same response to depend on earlier ids in that response, so that exclusive in-order execution satisfies existence checks.
38. As a captain, I want a missing dependency to still fail loud, so that a failed sibling create cannot leave a child pending forever.
39. As a member, I want claim and in_progress in the same response when Parallel Emission is on, so that I do not spend a step on the ritual.
40. As a member, I want completed and send_message in the same response when Parallel Emission is on, so that the captain is Woken once.
41. As a member already spawned, I want my persona unchanged when the checkbox flips, so that a mid-turn system prompt does not rewrite itself.
42. As a captain, I want the next assembled usage section to read the live checkbox, so that new turns pick up the opt-in without restart.
43. As a newly spawned member, I want my persona to match the checkbox at spawn, so that new workers and the captain agree.
44. As an assignment, I want Parallel Emission lines to match the live checkbox, so that the three protocol surfaces do not contradict.
45. As a user, I want serial protocol text when the checkbox is off, so that we do not MUST-parallel models that cannot emit multiple tools.
46. As a user, I want PR #48’s empty dependency branch rejected, so that tasks cannot hang on ids that never existed.
47. As a user, I want PR #48’s “never call status” rejected, so that Silent Kick and a diagnostic Probe remain available.
48. As a user, I want PR #48’s mandatory end-turn rejected, so that the captain can still guide.
49. As a user, I want no sleep-5-then-status protocol, so that we do not replace cache_read waste with wall-clock waste.
50. As a developer, I want lifecycle tests to drive due Next Probe At with a fake clock, so that ten minutes is not a real wait.
51. As a developer, I want offline verification to pin protocol strings for poll bans, panel independence, and Parallel Emission on/off, so that usage text cannot drift back to “Poll status until terminal”.
52. As a user, I want reduced-motion and hidden-page Activity View behaviour unchanged, so that probe work does not regress Issue #58 visuals.

## Implementation Decisions

- Extend the existing team scheduler rather than adding a watcher, HTTP route, or 1s scan of all teams. Fold due Next Probe At handling into Silent Kick (the current kick entry). Arm a single timer for the nearest due Next Probe At; cancel/recompute on Task Record writes.
- Store Next Probe At on the Task Record as an optional epoch-ms field. Absent means not armed. Attempt Start sets it to now + 10 minutes. Successful update_task for that attempt, terminal status, or a completion-shaped captain-bound message for that task id clears it. Captain Wake re-arms the same way as Attempt Start.
- Silent Kick is the current shared-task kick with no Captain Turn. After it, Captain Wake only if the Task Record is non-terminal and Member Liveness of the assignee is running, missing, or unknown. Idle + open work is left to the kick/retry already implemented on `agent/status` idle.
- Captain Wake and Mailbox Wake reuse the existing captain steer helper. If steer fails, leave the mailbox durable; do not tight-loop.
- Mailbox Wake: captain Agent Liveness idle/ready and unread captain mailbox. Independent of Next Probe At. Perform on kick paths and when mail is appended to the captain mailbox.
- Do not add a per-task Status Probe tool. Status Probe copy changes to: diagnostic snapshot and recovery kick; do not loop; Activity View already shows progress.
- create-task result copy notes that the scheduler notifies the assignee; do not send_message merely to dispatch.
- Protocol builders take Parallel Emission as a boolean. Captain usage section text is a function evaluated at assemble time. Member persona receives the flag only at spawn. Assignment prompt reads the live flag at dispatch.
- Settings namespace `agent-teams` with `parallelToolCalls: boolean` default false. Host registers the section when settings exist. Browser registers a Plugins-tab card keyed by that namespace (type-only slot contract; do not value-import another plugin’s card chrome). Checkbox label is product Chinese: 支持工具并行. Hint that this is Parallel Emission, that Agent Loop’s parallel cap is separate, and that cap 1 still runs exclusive tools in order in one step.
- Dependency existence checks stay. Same-response create_task relies on exclusive in-order execution.
- Inject a clock into the scheduler for tests. Do not use real 10-minute sleeps.
- Do not change Activity View polling cadence, visual status mapping, or maxParallelToolCalls.

Task Record shape addition (decision, not a file map):

```ts
interface TeamTask {
  // existing fields
  nextProbeAt?: number // epoch ms; absent = not armed
}
```

Due action (decision):

```
if due(task):
  Silent Kick
  if task non-terminal and assignee liveness in {running, missing, unknown}:
    Captain Wake
    re-arm nextProbeAt
  else:
    clear or leave to retry kick
```

## Testing Decisions

Good tests assert externally visible behaviour: Task Record fields after Attempt Start / update / complete; whether kick ran; whether captain steer ran; protocol strings for Parallel Emission on vs off; create_task still rejecting unknown dependency ids; settings default false.

- Scheduler / lifecycle harness (existing fake agents, tool execute, `agent/status` idle): arm, clear, Silent Kick without Wake for idle+open, Wake for running+open after due, re-arm after Wake, Mailbox Wake on unread + idle captain, fake clock.
- Offline `verify` string/contract checks: usage forbids “Poll status until terminal”; mentions Activity View independence; Parallel Emission on/off branches; create_task still throws on missing dependency.
- Settings: schema default false; card registers under the `agent-teams` namespace key when the Host serves that namespace.
- Do not require a full LLM e2e to prove prompt compliance; runtime clocks and string contracts are the seam. Optional later: one recorded team run with Parallel Emission off.

Prior art: `scripts/lifecycle-verify.mjs` (kick, idle retry, mailbox fallback), `scripts/verify.mjs` (pure protocol/source contracts), `scripts/stress-verify.mjs` (do not weaken).

## Out of Scope

- Merging or cherry-picking PR #48 as written.
- Changing Agent Loop `maxParallelToolCalls` or auto-detecting model multi-tool support.
- Rewriting personas of members already spawned.
- A per-task status tool, transcript scanning, or Activity View-driven probe clock.
- Making end-of-turn mandatory.
- Forward references to task ids that do not exist yet.
- User-configurable probe interval.
- Cold-restore of members while the captain Agent is offline (existing limitation), except Mailbox Wake when the captain Agent is present and idle.
- Visual/avatar/HMR work from Issue #58 except “do not regress”.

## Further Notes

Grilling settled this in-session (Q1–Q12, all recommended options). Glossary: `CONTEXT.md`. Upstream GitHub issues on NanmiCoder/dsh-agent-teams cannot be labelled by this checkout’s identity (read-only); keep this spec file as the source of record until someone with write access files it and applies `ready-for-agent`.

title: Feature proposal: reusable per-member tool policies (allow/deny)
body:
## Problem

AgentTeams already protects its Captain control plane by applying a hard-coded
`MEMBER_DENIED_TOOLS` filter when a member is spawned. Other than those six
Captain-only tools, however, every member sees the same global tool set.

This makes common role separation difficult. For example, a team owner cannot
declare that:

- a researcher may search and read, but not edit files or run shell commands;
- an implementer may edit and run commands;
- a reviewer may inspect diffs and run tests, but not modify the workspace.

DSH already supports this at the child-spawn seam: `toolFilter` accepts
`allow`/`deny`, hides filtered global tools from the child model, rejects their
execution, and is saved in the continuable subagent descriptor for cold
resume. AgentTeams already requires providers with the `toolFilter`
capability, so this should not require a DSH core change.

## Proposed first increment

Add reusable, configuration-owned **tool policies** and allow
`agent_teams_add_member` to select one by id.

The following TypeScript is illustrative rather than a request to commit to an
exact config spelling:

```ts
interface MemberToolPolicy {
  allow?: string[]
  deny?: string[]
}

interface Config {
  toolPolicies?: Record<string, MemberToolPolicy>
}
```

`agent_teams_add_member` would gain one optional model-facing field:

```ts
tool_policy?: string
```

The id must refer to a policy declared by the deployment owner. The model may
select an existing policy but may not submit raw `allow`/`deny` lists or
invent a new policy at runtime.

At member creation, one resolver would turn the selected policy into an
immutable effective filter. `spawnMember()` would receive only that resolved
filter and pass it to the existing `startContinuable()` call.

## Invariants

1. The existing Captain-only deny list always applies and cannot be undone by
   a policy.
2. The four member coordination tools required by the current persona remain
   available: `agent_teams_claim_task`, `agent_teams_update_task`,
   `agent_teams_send_message`, and `agent_teams_status`.
3. If a policy uses an allow-list, the effective allow-list explicitly
   includes those coordination tools; the effective deny-list is the union of
   the policy deny-list and the existing Captain-only deny-list.
4. Unknown policy ids and invalid/empty filters fail before a team member is
   persisted. If DSH rejects an unknown tool name during child creation, the
   existing no-orphan failure path remains intact.
5. `TeamMember` persists both the policy id and the resolved effective filter
   for status, audit, and recovery diagnostics. The DSH continuable descriptor
   remains the authority that reapplies the filter to a cold-resumed child.
6. Teams and members created without a policy retain the current v0.1.9
   behavior. Existing `team.json` files without the new fields remain valid.

## User-visible result

`agent_teams_status` should expose the selected policy id for each member. The
complete effective filter can remain in `team.json` for audit and diagnostics
instead of enlarging every status response. A UI editor is not needed in the
first increment; deployment configuration plus status output is enough to
make the behavior inspectable.

Example demo:

1. Configure `researcher` and `implementer` policies.
2. Add one member with each policy.
3. Show that the researcher does not receive write/shell tool schemas and that
   a forced call is rejected, while the implementer can use them.
4. Restart the Host and continue both members; their effective filters do not
   drift.

## Tests

- policy resolution and deterministic de-duplication;
- allow-list injection of the four coordination tools;
- Captain-only tools cannot be reintroduced through an allow-list;
- the resolved filter reaches the child spawn request, and denied tools are
  absent from the child's effective schema;
- unknown policy id and invalid filter fail without a persisted member or
  resumable orphan;
- `team.json` round-trip includes the policy snapshot;
- cold continuation retains the same filter;
- legacy team records and members without a policy preserve current behavior.

## Non-goals for the first PR

- No Settings or Activity Panel policy editor.
- No persona/template changes; this should stay separate from the preset
  persona work in PR #31.
- No per-turn or task-level policy mutation.
- No raw tool lists supplied by the Captain model.
- No claim that `toolFilter` is an OS sandbox or an authorization boundary; it
  is model tool visibility and invocation restriction for global tools.
- No support for subagent providers that do not advertise `toolFilter`.

## Open design questions

1. Is `toolPolicies` / `tool_policy` naming acceptable, or would the project
   prefer `memberPolicies` while still keeping persona/model concerns out of
   the first PR?
2. Should status expose the complete effective filter or only the policy id
   plus counts, with full details kept in `team.json`?
3. Should the initial PR support both `allow` and `deny`, or land deny-only
   first and add allow-lists once the required coordination-tool behavior is
   agreed?

If this direction fits the project, I can send a small Host/config/test PR
first and leave all UI work for a separate follow-up.

title: Feature: Add pluggable visual status indicators for all agents
body:
## Summary

Add a **generic visual-status layer** for AgentTeams agents. A design agent is a compelling first use case, but the data model and rendering mechanism should work for every agent role rather than becoming a design-agent-only feature.

When several agents are active, people should be able to recognize *who is working and what state they are in* without reading every task card.

## Proposed direction

1. Define a renderer-independent, semantic status model (for example: `idle`, `queued`, `planning`, `working`, `streaming`, `waiting_for_input`, `completed`, `failed`, and `cancelled`). Map the exact set to the AgentTeams lifecycle rather than exposing raw tool-call details.
2. Keep **identity** separate from **live state**: an agent can retain a stable avatar/seed, while a compact visual indicator communicates its current state.
3. Make the presentation extensible. The default can be an orb-like status indicator, but the status model should allow alternate renderers, themes, or agent-role-specific treatments later without changing the lifecycle data.
4. Use the existing UI state flow; do not add a separate polling loop solely for animation. Pause or throttle animation when the panel is hidden or collapsed, and clean up animation resources on unmount.
5. Keep the visual treatment accessible: always show a textual status, do not rely on color alone, provide an appropriate screen-reader label, and respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Visual references

These are inspiration references, **not** a request to copy the components or add a dependency:

- [Siri Orb](https://smoothui.dev/docs/components/siri-orb): a compact orb that makes semantic states such as idle, thinking, streaming, done, and error recognizable at a glance.
- [Agent Avatar](https://smoothui.dev/docs/components/agent-avatar): deterministic, distinct visuals that help users recognize individual agents in a team.
- [AI Orb Face](https://smoothui.dev/docs/components/ai-orb-face): an expressive alternative that makes activity states approachable while retaining explicit state labels.

A useful composition could be: **stable agent avatar for identity + small status orb/face for lifecycle state + text label for accessibility**. Design agents may use a richer visual treatment first, but other agents should receive the same generic state signal.

### Screenshots of the references

**Siri Orb**

![Screenshot of the SmoothUI Siri Orb reference](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/Elsen823/db7d49d1886e38e44f9cca28938dc335/raw/e5d3efb57291033d7d95fa07cc70d1771feeb1d9/smoothui-siri-orb.png)

**Agent Avatar**

![Screenshot of the SmoothUI Agent Avatar reference](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/Elsen823/db7d49d1886e38e44f9cca28938dc335/raw/e5d3efb57291033d7d95fa07cc70d1771feeb1d9/smoothui-agent-avatar.png)

**AI Orb Face**

![Screenshot of the SmoothUI AI Orb Face reference](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/Elsen823/db7d49d1886e38e44f9cca28938dc335/raw/e5d3efb57291033d7d95fa07cc70d1771feeb1d9/smoothui-ai-orb-face.png)

### README UI mockup using Agent Avatar

To make the proposal concrete, I made a lightweight mockup of the [current README UI screenshot](https://github.com/NanmiCoder/dsh-agent-teams/blob/main/assets/ui.png?raw=true) with the repeated agent icons simply replaced by the [Agent Avatar](https://smoothui.dev/docs/components/agent-avatar) component. The layout and text remain unchanged: each member gets a stable, visually distinct identity, while the small green completion indicator stays separate from the avatar.

This is only a visual substitution rather than a prescribed implementation or new dependency, but it shows that the existing surface can gain clearer agent identity with a small UI change. I hope this direction can be considered for adoption.

![AgentTeams README UI mockup using Agent Avatar](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/Elsen823/db7d49d1886e38e44f9cca28938dc335/raw/ed4c30bfd53dbe6748dd99648c92e1a201cfa7b9/dsh-agent-teams-agent-avatar-readme-mockup.png)

## Acceptance criteria

- A UI-facing, reusable status model exists and is not coupled to design-agent-specific fields.
- A default status renderer is visible in the AgentTeams activity surface and has a text equivalent for every state.
- The complete lifecycle, including waiting, completion, failure, and cancellation, has an intentional visual and text treatment.
- Motion honors `prefers-reduced-motion`; the UI remains understandable without animation or color.
- The implementation reuses the existing AgentTeams state updates and does not introduce a redundant continuous request loop.
- The renderer can be replaced or themed later without changing the lifecycle-to-status mapping.

## Scope note

The exact visual language is open for design. The goal is a general, accessible, and resource-conscious status presentation layer—not a hard dependency on any one reference component.

title: 插件模块导出的 name（`agent-teams`）与包名（`@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams`）不一致
body:
**问题**：`lib/index.js` 导出 `export const name = 'agent-teams'`，而 `package.json` 的 name 是 `@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams`，bundle patch 的 insert 行也是 `name: '@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams'`（`lib/types/index.d.ts` 同步）。

**影响**：host 以 `agent-teams` 注册插件，插件注册表与日志中的名字与真实包名脱节。当前不致命（工具注册/日志层面），但 Harness 新增的 `dsh plugin check` 会将其判为契约违例，且未来任何按插件名引用（patch 定向、遥测、会话归属）都会静默落空。

**契约**：模块导出的 `name` 必须等于 package.json 的 name（与 insert name / `__ModuleLoader__.load` id 的同一性规则同源）。

**修复建议**：改为 `export const name = '@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams'` 后发布（client 侧 `__ModuleLoader__.load` 的 id 已与 insert name 一致，无需改动）。

title: 通过消除 status 轮询和启用并行工具调用减少 token 浪费
body:
## 背景

通过对 AgentTeams 一次完整的"两首五言绝句 + 评审"任务的会话日志分析，发现 **ReAct 循环中存在大量不必要的 step**，每个 step 都要重读 ~15K 的 system prompt + 工具 schema（命中 cache_read），导致 token 消耗远超预期。

## 问题分析

### 会话日志实测数据（优化前）

| 会话 | 步数 | input | cache_read | output | 合计 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| captain | 14 | 26,311 | 215,040 | 1,948 | **243K** |
| poet-a | 7 | 20,527 | 83,968 | 1,758 | **106K** |
| poet-b | 6 | 16,334 | 71,680 | 1,075 | **89K** |
| critic | 7 | 19,470 | 88,064 | 2,106 | **110K** |
| **总计** | **34** | **82,642** | **458,752** | **6,887** | **548K** |

**88% 的 token 是 cache_read**（每步重读固定前缀），而真正的工作（input+output）只占 12%。

### 三类浪费

#### 1. status 轮询（captain 侧，~97K token）

captain 在创建任务后连续调用了 6 次 \`agent_teams_status\`，框架的 \`repeat-tool-reminder\` 插件已注入"Repeated tool call detected: consecutive_calls: 5"警告，但 captain 无视了：

\`\`\`
s5: status  ← 查一次（合理）
s6: status  ← 没新消息，再查
s7: status  ← 继续查
s8: status  ← 框架警告：repeating
s9: status  ← 仍然继续
s11: status ← sleep 之后又查
\`\`\`

每次 cache_read ~15K，6 次共浪费 ~97K token。

**根因**：captain persona 写了"monitor with agent_teams_status"和"Poll status until every required task is terminal"，直接鼓励轮询。

#### 2. 串行工具调用（member 侧，~84K token）

member 把本可并行的工具调用拆成了串行步骤：

\`\`\`
s3: claim_task              ← 拿 attempt_id
s4: update_task(in_progress) ← 等 s3 返回后才调
s5: update_task(completed)   ← 单独一步
s6: send_message             ← 等 s5 返回后才调
\`\`\`

实际上 \`claim_task\` 和 \`update_task(in_progress)\` 可以并行（DeepSeek API 支持单次返回多个 tool_calls，框架的 \`runGroup\` 也支持并行执行）。同理 \`update_task(completed)\` 和 \`send_message\` 也可以并行。

每个多余的 step 浪费 ~14K token，3 个 member 共浪费 ~84K。

**根因**：persona 用"Then mark in_progress"的措辞暗示了顺序执行；assignment prompt 说"call claim_task; it will return this same attempt_id"暗示需要先拿返回值。

#### 3. 收尾总结（双端，~37K token）

captain 在 \`delete\` 后输出了两步纯文本总结；member 在 \`send_message\` 后也输出了一步总结。这些步骤没有工具调用，纯粹是模型"礼貌收尾"。

\`\`\`
captain s13: (无工具) cache=18,432  output=364  ← 总结
captain s14: (无工具) cache=19,200  output=267  ← 二次总结
poet-a  s7: (无工具) cache=14,336  output=286  ← 收尾总结
\`\`\`

共浪费 ~37K token。

---

## 改动内容

4 个文件，10 行改动，分两层防御：

### captain 侧

#### \`src/index.ts\` — captain persona（3 处）

| 规则 | 旧 | 新 |
|---|---|---|
| 第 4 条 | "monitor with agent_teams_status" | "do NOT poll in a loop; use sleep; wait for member messages" |
| 第 6 条 | "Poll status until every required task is terminal" | "Wait for member completion messages instead of polling" |
| 第 7 条 | "Present results, then delete" | 追加"Do NOT output a recap or summary after delete" |

#### \`src/tools.ts\` — 工具描述 + 输出（2 处）

| 位置 | 旧 | 新 |
|---|---|---|
| \`status\` 描述 | "Poll this to watch progress" | "do NOT poll in a loop; members report completion automatically" |
| \`create_task\` 输出 | 只返回 task 信息 | 追加"The assignee has been auto-notified; do NOT call agent_teams_status to check" |

### member 侧

#### \`src/members.ts\` — member persona（4 处）

| 改动 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 禁止 status 轮询 | "Do NOT call agent_teams_status to poll for tasks — wait for messages" |
| claim + in_progress 并行 | "You may call claim_task and update_task(in_progress) in the SAME response" |
| completed + send_message 并行 | "You may call update_task(completed) and send_message in the SAME response" |
| 禁止收尾总结 | "After send_message, end your turn immediately. Do NOT output a summary" |

#### \`src/scheduler.ts\` — assignment prompt（1 处）

| 旧 | 新 |
|---|---|
| "call claim_task; it will return this same attempt_id" | 追加"You already know the attempt_id from this message, so you MAY call claim_task and update_task(in_progress) in the SAME response" |

关键点：assignment prompt 里已包含 \`attempt_id\`，member 不需要等 \`claim_task\` 返回就知道 attempt_id，因此可以并行调用。

---

## 防御层次

\`\`\`
captain 侧                              member 侧
┌───────────────────────┐              ┌───────────────────────┐
│ index.ts persona      │              │ members.ts persona    │
│ "不要轮询 status"      │              │ "不要查 status"        │
│ "用 sleep 等待"        │              │ "并行 claim+progress"  │
│ "delete 后不总结"      │              │ "并行 completed+msg"   │
└──────────┬────────────┘              │ "发完消息就结束"        │
           │                           └──────────┬────────────┘
           ▼                                      ▼
┌───────────────────────┐              ┌───────────────────────┐
│ tools.ts 描述/输出     │              │ scheduler.ts prompt   │
│ status: "不要循环"     │              │ "已知 attempt_id"      │
│ create_task: "已通知"  │              │ "可并行调用"           │
└───────────────────────┘              └───────────────────────┘
\`\`\`

每个角色都有两层防御：persona 层 + 工具/prompt 层。即使模型忽略了某一层，另一层仍能阻止浪费行为。

---

## 实测效果

### member 侧（已验证）

优化后重新运行了相同任务，对比日志：

| member | 旧版步数 | 新版步数 | 旧版 token | 新版 token | 降幅 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| poet-a | 7 | **4** | 106K | **60K** | **-44%** |
| poet-b | 6 | **4** | 89K | **60K** | **-33%** |
| judge | 7 | **6** | 110K | **78K** | **-29%** |
| **合计** | **20** | **14** | **305K** | **198K** | **-35%** |

三个优化全部生效：
- ✅ welcome 后不再查 status（省 1-2 步）
- ✅ claim + in_progress 并行（省 1 步）
- ✅ completed + send_message 并行（省 1 步）
- ⚠️ 收尾总结部分消除（output 从 286 降到 43，但仍有 1 步短收尾）

### captain 侧（预期）

未重新测试，但根据改动逻辑预期：

| | 旧版 | 预期新版 |
|---|---|---|
| 步数 | 14 | **7** |
| token | 241K | **~107K** |
| 降幅 | | **-55%** |

---

## 影响范围

| 场景 | 是否受影响 | 风险 |
|---|---|---|
| AgentTeams 任务（captain） | ✅ 行为变化 | 低：从轮询改为等消息，语义等价 |
| AgentTeams 任务（member） | ✅ 行为变化 | 低：并行调用不影响正确性，框架已支持 |
| 非 AgentTeams 会话 | ✅ system prompt 增加 ~50 token | 可忽略 |

\`index.ts\` 的 persona 是全局注入的，但只在用户主动要求用 AgentTeams 时生效（persona 开头有"When the user asks to run something with AgentTeams"守卫）。

---

## 测试

\`\`\`bash
npm test
npm run lint
\`\`\`

title: feat: add focus mode to reduce human interruption
body:
# feat: add focus mode to reduce human interruption

## Summary

- Add a new `focusMode` config option (default `false`, opt-in) to dsh-agent-teams.
- When enabled, the captain system prompt includes a Focus Protocol:
  - Ask the captain to notify the user only on completion, failure, or a decision that genuinely needs the user.
  - Ask the captain to keep the human-visible task list short and push background work to autonomous agents.
  - Ask the captain not to start extra deep tasks while agents are running, and to batch the final summary.
  - Ask the captain to mark blocked/needs-decision tasks once and wait.
- When `focusMode: false`, the previous always-report prompt behavior is preserved.

## Motivation

Running multiple agents in parallel increases context-switching cost. This feature lets users keep AgentTeams running in the background without being interrupted by progress chatter, matching the “only notify on completion/failure/needs-decision” pattern from AI multitasking/focus guidance.

## Scope / Limitation

- This is a **prompt-level guideline**, not a hard notification filter.
- It changes what the captain is instructed to do; a model may still surface important updates.
- A future follow-up could add a real delivery filter at the scheduler/mailbox layer.

## Test Plan

- [x] `pnpm typecheck`
- [x] `pnpm build`
- [x] `pnpm verify` (offline + lifecycle + stress)
- [x] Manual config check: `focusMode: true` adds Focus Protocol to the system prompt section; `focusMode: false` keeps original text

## Notes

- Default is `false` (opt-in) to preserve existing behavior.

title: fix: add session-log migration tool for pre-0.1.0 logs (Fixes #19)
body:
Fixes #19 — 存量会话日志迁移工具。

## 背景

0.1.0 及更早版本（以及 #8 修复前的本地构建）写入会话日志的 `agent-teams/*` 事件没有携带 `ignorable` 信封标记。harness 的持久化协调器会拒绝解释任何包含"未知且未标记 ignorable"事件类型的日志：

```
SessionFormatUnsupportedError: ... contains event type "agent-teams/task-created" ...
unknown to this harness and not marked ignorable; refusing to interpret the log
```

#8/#9 修复了**新写入**，但存量会话的日志仍然打不开，#19 请求提供迁移工具。

## 改动

- `scripts/migrate-session-logs.mjs`（新增，零依赖，仅 Node 内置 zstd）：
  - 解码日志的每个 Zstandard 帧（按 harness JSONL 后端的帧布局扫描）
  - 只给缺失标记的 `agent-teams/*` 事件插入 `"ignorable": true`，其余字节原样保留
  - 以"头帧 + 单 body 帧"重新编码（与 harness 读取器兼容，checksum 与写入端一致）
  - **幂等**：无缺失标记的日志原样不动（不产生写入）
  - 结构校验：损坏/撕裂帧会报错而不是静默改写
  - 内置 `--self-test`：内存构造合成日志验证插入与幂等性
- `README.md`：新增「存量日志迁移」章节，给出 `find ... -exec` 一键迁移命令与自检方式

## 验证

- `node scripts/migrate-session-logs.mjs --self-test` 通过
- 用真实的历史损坏日志（3 条未标记事件）实测：修补成功、无残留未标记事件、首帧合法、二次运行 no-op

title: [反馈] agent-teams/* 事件导致历史会话重启后无法加载：确认 0.1.0 已修复，但存量会话建议提供迁移工具
body:
# [反馈] agent-teams/* 会话事件导致历史会话加载失败（SessionFormatUnsupportedError）——确认 0.1.0 修复有效，但存量会话无法自动恢复

## 现象

使用 agent-teams 创建过团队的会话，在 web 服务重启后无法打开，报：

```
SessionFormatUnsupportedError: session "…" contains event type "agent-teams/team-created" (seq …)
unknown to this harness and not marked ignorable; refusing to interpret the log —
it was likely written by a newer harness (raw log: …/session.jsonl.zstd)
```

会话日志里包含的 `agent-teams/*` 事件（`team-created` / `member-added` / `member-removed` / `task-created` / `task-updated` / `message-sent` / `team-deleted`）不在 DSH 内核 `KNOWN_SESSION_EVENT_TYPES`（43 个内置类型）中；内核的 `dsh-session-persistence` 读取路径 `assertEventsSupported()` 会拒绝解析整份日志，除非事件带 `ignorable: true` 标记。

## 根因（已确认）

1. **DSH 内核无插件事件类型注册机制**。`dsh-session` 的 `KNOWN_SESSION_EVENT_TYPES` 是生成后硬编码的集合，源码注释明确："a registration surface for them is deferred until such a consumer exists"。
2. **`Session.append()` 不透传 `ignorable`**。实测 dsh@0.1.0-rc.6：`session.append(type, data, { ignorable: true })` 产生的事件对象只有 `type/seq/time/data` 四个键，opts 中的 `ignorable` 被静默丢弃。
3. 因此旧版插件每次 `appendTeamEvent()` 写入的 `agent-teams/*` 事件都是"未知且不可忽略"的——只要 web 服务重启、会话从磁盘重放，就会整份失败。

## 上游已做的修复（确认有效）

- PR #1（mitao-su）曾尝试在插件 apply 时把 7 个类型注册进 `KNOWN_SESSION_EVENT_TYPES`（feature-detected，幂等）。
- 后续 harden commit（`18701c99`）改为更保守的方案并已发布到 npm `0.1.0`：`appendTeamEvent()` 先检查 `KNOWN_SESSION_EVENT_TYPES.has(type)`，不认识的类型**直接不写日志**（`skippedEventTypes` 去重 + debug 日志），保留磁盘 team 状态（`<stateDir>/<teamId>/team.json` + inbox）作为活动面板的权威来源。

结论：**升级到 0.1.0 / main 后，新建会话不再产生 `agent-teams/*` 日志事件，不会再触发加载失败**。本机已升级并验证。

## 遗留问题（建议作者考虑）

1. **存量会话无法自动恢复**。修复只停止"写入"，已写入 `agent-teams/*` 事件的旧会话日志仍会被内核拒绝。升级插件不会改写历史日志，这些会话（即便取消归档）依然打不开。可选方案：
   - 提供一次性迁移工具：扫描会话日志，把 `agent-teams/*` 事件行改写为 `"ignorable": true`（或移除），再重新压缩为 checksummed zstd 帧；
   - 或在插件里提供"只读修复"命令，在加载前先对旧日志做兼容处理。
2. **活动面板数据来源依赖 disk state 目录**。`omit` 后会话日志不再是活动面板的权威来源，依赖 `<stateDir>` 目录存活；若该目录被清理，历史团队视图会丢失。建议在 README 中说明团队状态的生命周期与备份方式。

## 环境信息
